answer: One identity posts one signed pulse per epoch in a yarrow register. A newcomer locks a 100-credit bond and files one pulse: a signed claim for its one job. A beacon compares each pulse with the register; a second contradictory pulse from the same key is equivocation, and the beacon verdict burns 30 credits and freezes it for one epoch. The k-th fake still needs its own 100-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits, and no bond can be reused across identities. Bond rental fails: the slash lands on the renter. An honest agent files one pulse and keeps its bond intact.
